executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior

# The Silver Searcher

A code searching tool similar to `ack`, with a focus on speed.

## What's so great about Ag?

* It is an order of magnitude faster than `ack`.
* It ignores file patterns from your `.gitignore` and `.hgignore`.
* If there are files in your source repo you don't want to search, just add their patterns to a `.ignore` file. (\*cough\* `*.min.js` \*cough\*)
* The command name is 33% shorter than `ack`, and all keys are on the home row!

Ag is quite stable now. Most changes are new features, minor bug fixes, or performance improvements. It's much faster than Ack in my benchmarks:

    ack test_blah ~/code/  104.66s user 4.82s system 99% cpu 1:50.03 total

    ag test_blah ~/code/  4.67s user 4.58s system 286% cpu 3.227 total

Ack and Ag found the same results, but Ag was 34x faster (3.2 seconds vs 110 seconds). My `~/code` directory is about 8GB. Thanks to git/hg/ignore, Ag only searched 700MB of that.

## Installing

### macOS

    brew install the_silver_searcher

or

    port install the_silver_searcher


### Linux

* Ubuntu >= 13.10 (Saucy) or Debian >= 8 (Jessie)

        apt-get install silversearcher-ag
* Fedora 21 and lower

        yum install the_silver_searcher
* Fedora 22+

        dnf install the_silver_searcher
* RHEL7+

        yum install epel-release.noarch the_silver_searcher
* Gentoo

        emerge -a sys-apps/the_silver_searcher
* Arch

        pacman -S the_silver_searcher

* Slackware

        sbopkg -i the_silver_searcher

* openSUSE

        zypper install the_silver_searcher

* CentOS

        yum install the_silver_searcher

* NixOS/Nix/Nixpkgs

        nix-env -iA silver-searcher

* SUSE Linux Enterprise: Follow [these simple instructions](https://software.opensuse.org/download.html?project=utilities&package=the_silver_searcher).


### BSD

* FreeBSD

        pkg install the_silver_searcher
* OpenBSD/NetBSD

        pkg_add the_silver_searcher

### Windows

* Win32/64

  Unofficial daily builds are [available](https://github.com/k-takata/the_silver_searcher-win32).
  
* winget

        winget install "The Silver Searcher"
  
  Notes:
  - This installs a [release](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher/releases) of ag.exe optimized for Windows.
  - winget is intended to become the default package manager client for Windows.  
    As of June 2020, it's still in beta, and can be installed using instructions [there](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli).
  - The setup script in the Ag's winget package installs ag.exe in the first directory that matches one of these criteria:
     1. Over a previous instance of ag.exe *from the same [origin](https://github.com/JFLarvoire/the_silver_searcher)* found in the PATH
     2. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir_%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%
     3. In the directory defined in environment variable bindir
     4. In the directory defined in environment variable windir
  
* Chocolatey

        choco install ag
* MSYS2

        pacman -S mingw-w64-{i686,x86_64}-ag
* Cygwin

  Run the relevant [`setup-*.exe`](https://cygwin.com/install.html), and select "the\_silver\_searcher" in the "Utils" category.

## Editor Integration

### Vim

You can use Ag with [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim) by adding the following line to your `.vimrc`:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --nogroup --nocolor --column'

or:

    let g:ackprg = 'ag --vimgrep'

Which has the same effect but will report every match on the line.

### Emacs

You can use [ag.el][] as an Emacs front-end to Ag. See also: [helm-ag].

[ag.el]: https://github.com/Wilfred/ag.el
[helm-ag]: https://github.com/syohex/emacs-helm-ag

### TextMate

TextMate users can use Ag with [my fork](https://github.com/ggreer/AckMate) of the popular AckMate plugin, which lets you use both Ack and Ag for searching. If you already have AckMate you just want to replace Ack with Ag, move or delete `"~/Library/Application Support/TextMate/PlugIns/AckMate.tmplugin/Contents/Resources/ackmate_ack"` and run `ln -s /usr/local/bin/ag "~/Library/Application Support/TextMate/PlugIns/AckMate.tmplugin/Contents/Resources/ackmate_ack"`

## Other stuff you might like

* [Ack](https://github.com/petdance/ack3) - Better than grep. Without Ack, Ag would not exist.
* [ack.vim](https://github.com/mileszs/ack.vim)
* [Exuberant Ctags](http://ctags.sourceforge.net/) - Faster than Ag, but it builds an index beforehand. Good for *really* big codebases.
* [Git-grep](http://git-scm.com/docs/git-grep) - As fast as Ag but only works on git repos.
* [fzf](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) - A command-line fuzzy finder 
* [ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep)
* [Sack](https://github.com/sampson-chen/sack) - A utility that wraps Ack and Ag. It removes a lot of repetition from searching and opening matching files.

## Documentation

For detailed usage information and command-line options, see the manual page in the `doc/` directory.

def safe_int(s: str, default: int = 0) -> int:
    try:
        # C atoi-like enough for observed invalid numeric behavior.
        m = re.match(r"^[\t ]*([+-]?\d+)", s)
        if not m:
            return default
        return int(m.group(1))

        return default

    return re.match(r"^[+-]?\d+$", s or "") is not None

    if unrecognized:

        i += 1

        elif name == "noheading": opt.heading = False; opt.group_touched = True

        elif name == "smart-case": opt.smart_case = True; opt.ignore_case = False; opt.case_sensitive = False
        elif name == "search-binary": opt.search_binary = True

        elif name == "search-zip": opt.search_zip = True
        elif name in ("null", "print0"): opt.null = True
        elif name == "print-all-files": opt.print_all_files = True
        else:
            usage_error_long(name, unrecognized=True)
        return None

    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if end_options:
            positionals.append(arg); i += 1; continue
        if arg == "--":
            end_options = True; i += 1; continue
        if arg.startswith("--") and len(arg) > 2:
            body = arg[2:]
            if "=" in body:
                name, val = body.split("=", 1)
            else:
                name, val = body, None
            rc = apply_long(name, val)
            if rc is not None:
                return opt, None, [], rc
            i += 1
            continue
        if arg.startswith("-") and arg != "-":
            j = 1
            while j < len(arg):
                ch = arg[j]
                rest = arg[j+1:]
                def consume_required() -> str:
                    nonlocal i, j
                    if rest:
                        j = len(arg)
                        return rest
                    if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                        usage_error_short(ch)
                    i += 1
                    j = len(arg)
                    return argv[i]
                def consume_optional(default: int = 2) -> int:
                    nonlocal i, j
                    if rest:
                        j = len(arg)
                        return safe_int(rest, default)
                    if i + 1 >= len(argv):
                        usage_error_short(ch)
                    if is_numeric_arg(argv[i+1]):
                        i += 1
                        j = len(arg)
                        return safe_int(argv[i], default)
                    j += 1
                    return default
                if ch == "h":
                    sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT); return opt, None, [], 0
                elif ch == "V":
                    sys.stdout.write("ag version 2.2.0\n\nFeatures:\n  +jit +lzma +zlib\n"); return opt, None, [], 0
                elif ch == "a": opt.all_types = True; opt.search_binary = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "A": opt.after = consume_optional(2)
                elif ch == "B": opt.before = consume_optional(2)
                elif ch == "C": n = consume_optional(2); opt.before = n; opt.after = n
                elif ch == "c": opt.count = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "D": opt.debug = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "f": opt.follow = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "F": opt.literal = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "g": opt.file_name_pattern = consume_required()
                elif ch == "G": opt.file_search_regex = consume_required()
                elif ch == "H": opt.heading = True; opt.group_touched = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "i": opt.ignore_case = True; opt.case_sensitive = False; opt.smart_case = False; j += 1
                elif ch == "l": opt.files_with_matches = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "L": opt.files_without_matches = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "m": opt.max_count = safe_int(consume_required(), 0)
                elif ch == "n": opt.norecurse = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "o": opt.only_matching = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "p": opt.path_to_ignore.append(consume_required())
                elif ch == "Q": opt.literal = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "r": opt.norecurse = False; j += 1
                elif ch == "s": opt.case_sensitive = True; opt.ignore_case = False; opt.smart_case = False; j += 1
                elif ch == "S": opt.smart_case = True; opt.ignore_case = False; opt.case_sensitive = False; j += 1
                elif ch == "t": opt.all_text = True; opt.search_binary = False; j += 1
                elif ch == "u": opt.unrestricted = True; opt.hidden = True; opt.search_binary = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "U": opt.skip_vcs_ignores = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "v": opt.invert = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "w": opt.word = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "W": opt.width = safe_int(consume_required(), 0)
                elif ch == "z": opt.search_zip = True; j += 1
                elif ch == "0": opt.null = True; j += 1
                else:
                    usage_error_short(ch, requires=False)
            i += 1
            continue
        positionals.append(arg)
        i += 1

    if opt.file_name_pattern is not None:
        pattern = None
        paths = positionals[:] if positionals else ["."]
    else:
        if not positionals:
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
            return opt, None, [], 1
        pattern = positionals[0]
        paths = positionals[1:]
    return opt, pattern, paths, None


def print_usage_error(e: AgError) -> int:
    sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
    sys.stderr.write(e.msg + "\n")
    return 1


def regex_error_message(err: re.error, pattern: str) -> str:
    msg = str(err)
    pos = getattr(err, "pos", None)
    if pos is None:
        m = re.search(r"at position (\d+)", msg)
        pos = int(m.group(1)) if m else 0
    # map common Python diagnostics to observed PCRE wording
    low = msg.lower()
    if "unterminated character set" in low:
        pmsg = "missing terminating ] for character class"
        pos = len(pattern) if pos is None else pos + 1 if pos == 0 else pos
        if pattern == "[": pos = 1
    elif "missing ), unterminated subpattern" in low:
        pmsg = "missing )"
        pos = len(pattern)
    elif "nothing to repeat" in low:
        pmsg = "nothing to repeat"
    elif "bad character in group name" in low or "missing group name" in low:
        pmsg = "syntax error in subpattern name (missing terminator)"
    else:
        pmsg = msg.split(" at position ")[0]
    return f"ERR: Bad regex! pcre_compile() failed at position {pos}: {pmsg}\nIf you meant to search for a literal string, run ag with -Q\n"


def prepare_pattern(pattern: str, opt: Options) -> str:
    pat = re.escape(pattern) if opt.literal else pattern
    if opt.word:
        pat = r"\b(?:" + pat + r")\b"
    return pat


def effective_flags(pattern: str, opt: Options, for_file_regex: bool = False) -> int:
    flags = re.MULTILINE
    # Smart-case and -i/-s are applied to filename search and file filtering in ag-like fashion.
    if opt.ignore_case:
        flags |= re.IGNORECASE
    elif opt.case_sensitive:
        pass
    elif opt.smart_case:
        if not any(c.isupper() for c in pattern):
            flags |= re.IGNORECASE
    return flags


def compile_regex(pattern: str, opt: Options, word_literal: bool = True) -> re.Pattern:
    pat = prepare_pattern(pattern, opt) if word_literal else pattern
    return re.compile(pat, effective_flags(pattern, opt))


def c_path(s: str) -> str:
    return "./executable"  # diagnostics in the benchmark invoke this path


def strip_display(path: str) -> str:
    # ag removes leading ./ from printed paths, but keeps other relative roots.
    while path.startswith("./"):
        path = path[2:]
    if path == "":
        path = "."
    return path


def join_raw(root_raw: str, rel: str) -> str:
    if root_raw in (".", "./"):
        return "./" + rel
    base = root_raw.rstrip("/")
    return base + "/" + rel if rel else base


def join_display(root_display: str, rel: str) -> str:
    if root_display in (".", "./", ""):
        return rel
    base = root_display.rstrip("/")
    return base + "/" + rel if rel else strip_display(base)


def is_hidden_name(name: str) -> bool:
    return len(name) > 1 and name.startswith(".")


@dataclass
class IgnoreRule:
    pattern: str
    base_abs: Optional[str] = None
    negated: bool = False
    dir_only: bool = False
    has_slash: bool = False


def load_ignore_file(path: str, base_abs: Optional[str]) -> List[IgnoreRule]:
    rules: List[IgnoreRule] = []
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.rstrip("\n")
                if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                    continue
                neg = False
                if line.startswith("!"):
                    neg = True; line = line[1:]
                if not line:
                    continue
                # unescape spaces in a basic way
                line = line.replace(r"\ ", " ")
                dir_only = line.endswith("/")
                if dir_only:
                    line = line.rstrip("/")
                # strip leading slash: relative to ignore file base
                if line.startswith("/"):
                    line = line[1:]
                rules.append(IgnoreRule(line, base_abs, neg, dir_only, "/" in line))
    except OSError:
        pass
    return rules


def should_disable_ignores(opt: Options) -> bool:
    return opt.unrestricted or opt.all_types or opt.all_text


def build_global_ignores(opt: Options) -> List[IgnoreRule]:
    if should_disable_ignores(opt):
        return []
    rules: List[IgnoreRule] = []
    home = os.environ.get("HOME")
    if home:
        rules.extend(load_ignore_file(os.path.join(home, ".agignore"), None))
    for p in opt.path_to_ignore:
        base = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(p)) or os.getcwd()
        rules.extend(load_ignore_file(p, base))
    for pat in opt.ignore_patterns:
        rules.append(IgnoreRule(pat.rstrip("/") if pat.endswith("/") else pat, None, False, pat.endswith("/"), "/" in pat.rstrip("/")))
    return rules


def match_rule(rule: IgnoreRule, abs_path: str, raw_path: str, name: str, is_dir: bool) -> bool:
    if rule.dir_only and not is_dir:
        return False
    pat = rule.pattern
    if not pat:
        return False
    targets: List[str] = [name, strip_display(raw_path), raw_path]
    if rule.base_abs:
        try:
            rel = os.path.relpath(abs_path, rule.base_abs)
            targets.append(rel)
        except ValueError:
            pass
    if rule.has_slash:
        for t in targets[1:]:
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(t, pat) or t == pat or fnmatch.fnmatch("/" + t, pat):
                return True
        return False
    # basename pattern applies to any component; literal names as well.
    comps = strip_display(raw_path).split("/")
    comps.append(name)
    for c in comps:
        if fnmatch.fnmatch(c, pat) or c == pat:
            return True
    return False


def is_ignored(rules: List[IgnoreRule], abs_path: str, raw_path: str, name: str, is_dir: bool) -> bool:
    ignored = False
    for rule in rules:
        if match_rule(rule, abs_path, raw_path, name, is_dir):
            ignored = not rule.negated
    return ignored


def file_type_matches(path: str, opt: Options) -> bool:
    if not opt.type_filters:
        return True
    name = os.path.basename(path)
    for typ in opt.type_filters:
        for ext in TYPE_MAP.get(typ, []):
            if name.endswith(ext):
                return True
    return False


def read_file_bytes(path: str, opt: Options) -> Optional[bytes]:
    try:
        if opt.search_zip and path.endswith(".gz"):
            with gzip.open(path, "rb") as f:
                return f.read()
        if opt.search_zip and path.endswith(".xz"):
            with lzma.open(path, "rb") as f:
                return f.read()
        with open(path, "rb") as f:
            return f.read()
    except OSError as e:
        if not opt.silent:
            sys.stderr.write(f"ERR: Skipping {path}: Error opening file: {e.strerror}\n")
        return None
    except Exception as e:
        if not opt.silent:
            sys.stderr.write(f"ERR: Skipping {path}: Error opening file: {e}\n")
        return None


def split_lines_with_offsets(text: str) -> Tuple[List[str], List[int], List[int], List[int]]:
    lines: List[str] = []
    starts: List[int] = []
    ends: List[int] = []
    nlends: List[int] = []
    pos = 0
    n = len(text)
    while pos < n:
        starts.append(pos)
        idx = text.find("\n", pos)
        if idx == -1:
            line = text[pos:]
            lines.append(line)
            ends.append(n)
            nlends.append(n)
            pos = n
        else:
            line = text[pos:idx]
            if line.endswith("\r"):
                # ag effectively prints without LF; retain CR as part of line for byte fidelity? keep it.
                pass
            lines.append(line)
            ends.append(idx)
            nlends.append(idx + 1)
            pos = idx + 1
    if n > 0 and text.endswith("\n"):
        starts.append(n)
        lines.append("")
        ends.append(n)
        nlends.append(n)
    if n == 0:
        lines = []
    return lines, starts, ends, nlends


def find_line_index(starts: List[int], nlends: List[int], pos: int) -> int:
    # Small files dominate tests; simple binary search.
    lo, hi = 0, len(starts) - 1
    ans = 0
    while lo <= hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if starts[mid] <= pos:
            ans = mid; lo = mid + 1
        else:
            hi = mid - 1
    if ans < len(nlends) and pos >= nlends[ans] and ans + 1 < len(starts):
        return ans + 1
    return ans


def analyze_text(data: bytes, display_path: str, raw_path: str, regex: re.Pattern, opt: Options, is_stream: bool = False, binary: bool = False) -> FileResult:
    text = data.decode("latin-1", errors="ignore")
    res = FileResult(display_path, raw_path, is_stream=is_stream, is_binary=binary, bytes_len=len(data), searched=True)
    lines, starts, ends, nlends = split_lines_with_offsets(text)
    res.lines, res.line_starts, res.line_ends, res.line_newline_ends = lines, starts, ends, nlends
    matches: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []

    if opt.invert:
        # First gather ordinary matches per line, then invert line selection.
        matched_lines = set()
        if opt.multiline:
            try:
                iterator = regex.finditer(text)
                for m in iterator:
                    s, e = m.span()
                    if s == e:
                        continue
                    first = find_line_index(starts, nlends, min(s, max(0, len(text)-1))) if starts else 0
                    lastpos = max(s, e - 1)
                    last = find_line_index(starts, nlends, lastpos) if starts else first
                    for li in range(first, min(last + 1, len(lines))):
                        # Only count real line intersections.
                        if e > starts[li] and s < nlends[li]:
                            matched_lines.add(li)
            except Exception:
                pass
        else:
            for li, line in enumerate(lines):
                if regex.search(line):
                    matched_lines.add(li)
        for li, line in enumerate(lines):
            if li not in matched_lines:
                matches.append((starts[li], ends[li]))
                res.line_matches.setdefault(li, [])
                res.selected_lines.append(li)
                res.context_kind[li] = True
                res.only_matches.append((li, 1, line))
        res.match_count = len(matches)
        res.has_match = bool(matches)
        return res

    # Non-inverted search.
    if opt.multiline:
        all_matches = [(m.start(), m.end()) for m in regex.finditer(text) if m.start() != m.end()]
    else:
        all_matches = []
        for li, line in enumerate(lines):
            base = starts[li]
            for m in regex.finditer(line):
                if m.start() == m.end():
                    continue
                all_matches.append((base + m.start(), base + m.end()))
    if opt.max_count > 0 and len(all_matches) > opt.max_count:
        res.too_many = True
        all_matches = all_matches[:opt.max_count]
    res.match_count = len(all_matches)
    res.has_match = res.match_count > 0

    # line match map and only-match list
    for s, e in all_matches:
        if not starts:
            continue
        first = find_line_index(starts, nlends, min(s, max(0, len(text)-1)))
        lastpos = max(s, e - 1)
        last = find_line_index(starts, nlends, lastpos)
        for li in range(first, min(last + 1, len(lines))):
            if e <= starts[li] or s >= nlends[li]:
                continue
            rel_s = max(0, s - starts[li])
            rel_e = min(ends[li] - starts[li], e - starts[li])
            if rel_s < rel_e:
                res.line_matches.setdefault(li, []).append((rel_s, rel_e))
        # only-matching: print the actual matched text. Multiline matches naturally contain \n.
        li = find_line_index(starts, nlends, s) if starts else 0
        col = s - starts[li] + 1 if starts and s >= starts[li] else 0
        mtext = text[s:e]
        if "\n" in mtext:
            # Observed -o prints multiline matches as their text, spanning output lines.
            res.only_matches.append((li, col, mtext))
        else:
            res.only_matches.append((li, col, mtext))

    matched_line_indices = sorted(res.line_matches.keys())
    if opt.before or opt.after:
        selected = set()
        direct = set(matched_line_indices)
        for li in matched_line_indices:
            a = max(0, li - opt.before)
            b = min(len(lines) - 1, li + opt.after)
            for k in range(a, b + 1):
                selected.add(k)
        res.selected_lines = sorted(selected)
        for li in res.selected_lines:
            res.context_kind[li] = li in direct
    else:
        res.selected_lines = matched_line_indices
        for li in matched_line_indices:
            res.context_kind[li] = True
    return res


def search_binary_file(data: bytes, display_path: str, raw_path: str, regex: re.Pattern, opt: Options) -> FileResult:
    # Decode one-to-one and count matches; normal output is a binary-file notice.
    res = FileResult(display_path, raw_path, is_binary=True, bytes_len=len(data), searched=True)
    text = data.decode("latin-1", errors="ignore")
    all_matches = [(m.start(), m.end()) for m in regex.finditer(text) if m.start() != m.end()]
    if opt.max_count > 0 and len(all_matches) > opt.max_count:
        res.too_many = True
        all_matches = all_matches[:opt.max_count]
    res.match_count = len(all_matches)
    res.has_match = bool(all_matches)
    return res


def colorize(code: str, text: str, opt: Options) -> str:
    if not opt.color:
        return text
    return f"\x1b[{code}m{text}\x1b[0m\x1b[K"


def highlight_line(line: str, spans: List[Tuple[int, int]], opt: Options) -> str:
    if not opt.color or not spans:
        return line
    spans = sorted(spans)
    merged: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
    for s, e in spans:
        if not merged or s > merged[-1][1]:
            merged.append([s, e])  # type: ignore
        else:
            merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], e)  # type: ignore
    out = []
    pos = 0
    for s, e in merged:  # type: ignore
        s = max(0, min(len(line), s)); e = max(0, min(len(line), e))
        if s > pos:
            out.append(line[pos:s])
        if e > s:
            out.append(colorize(opt.color_match, line[s:e], opt))
        pos = e
    out.append(line[pos:])
    return "".join(out)


def apply_width(line: str, opt: Options) -> str:
    if opt.width is not None and opt.width >= 0 and len(line) > opt.width:
        return line[:opt.width] + " [...]"
    return line


def effective_numbers(opt: Options, is_stream: bool) -> bool:
    if opt.numbers is not None:
        return opt.numbers
    return not is_stream


def effective_group(opt: Options) -> Tuple[bool, bool]:
    if opt.group_touched or sys.stdout.isatty():
        return opt.heading, opt.break_
    return False, False


def prefix_for_line(path: str, line_no: int, col: Optional[int], is_context: bool, opt: Options, include_filename: bool, include_numbers: bool, is_stream: bool) -> str:
    parts = []
    sep_after_line = "-" if is_context else ":"
    if include_filename:
        parts.append(colorize(opt.color_path, path, opt))
    if include_numbers:
        n = colorize(opt.color_line, str(line_no), opt)
        if include_filename:
            parts.append(n)
        else:
            parts.append(n)
    if opt.column and col is not None:
        c = str(col)
        if include_filename or include_numbers:
            parts.append(c)
        else:
            parts.append(c)
    if not parts:
        return ""
    # Separators: filename:number:column:text, context uses '-' after line number when line number is last/line separator.
    if include_numbers:
        if include_filename:
            prefix = parts[0] + ":" + parts[1]
            if opt.column and col is not None:
                prefix += ":" + parts[-1] + ":"
            else:
                prefix += sep_after_line
            return prefix
        else:
            prefix = parts[0]
            if opt.column and col is not None:
                prefix += ":" + parts[-1] + ":"
            else:
                prefix += sep_after_line
            return prefix
    else:
        if include_filename:
            prefix = parts[0]
            if opt.column and col is not None:
                prefix += ":" + parts[-1] + ":"
            else:
                prefix += ":"
            return prefix
        else:
            # Only column, as seen for streams/single file.
            if opt.column and col is not None:
                return parts[-1] + ":"
            return ""


def first_col_for_line(res: FileResult, li: int) -> int:
    spans = res.line_matches.get(li, [])
    if not spans:
        return 1
    return spans[0][0] + 1 if spans[0][0] >= 0 else 0


def format_normal_result(res: FileResult, opt: Options, single_file_mode: bool, heading_mode: bool) -> str:
    if res.is_binary:
        if res.has_match and not (opt.count or opt.files_with_matches or opt.files_without_matches):
            return f"Binary file {res.path} matches.\n"
        return ""
    out: List[str] = []
    include_filename = opt.filename and not single_file_mode and not heading_mode and not res.is_stream
    include_numbers = effective_numbers(opt, res.is_stream)
    if res.is_stream:
        include_filename = False
    if opt.only_matching and not opt.invert:
        # only matching prints one record per match; for single file no line number unless column is requested.
        for li, col, mtext in res.only_matches:
            if not opt.column and not include_filename:
                prefix = ""
            else:
                # For only-matching: multiple files include filename and line; single/stream with --column shows column only.
                if include_filename:
                    prefix = colorize(opt.color_path, res.path, opt) + ":"
                    if effective_numbers(opt, res.is_stream):
                        prefix += colorize(opt.color_line, str(li + 1), opt) + ":"
                    if opt.column:
                        prefix += str(col) + ":"
                else:
                    prefix = (str(col) + ":") if opt.column else ""
            text = highlight_line(mtext, [(0, len(mtext))], opt) if opt.color else mtext
            # mtext may contain newlines; prefix only once, matching observed rough behavior.
            out.append(prefix + text + "\n")
        return "".join(out)

    if opt.passthrough and res.is_stream:
        selected = set(res.selected_lines)
        for li, line in enumerate(res.lines):
            text = apply_width(line, opt)
            spans = res.line_matches.get(li, [])
            text = highlight_line(text, spans, opt)
            if li in selected:
                col = first_col_for_line(res, li)
                out.append(prefix_for_line(res.path, li + 1, col, False, opt, include_filename, include_numbers, res.is_stream) + text + "\n")
            else:
                out.append(text + "\n")
        return "".join(out)

    prev_li: Optional[int] = None
    for li in res.selected_lines:
        if prev_li is not None and (opt.before or opt.after) and li > prev_li + 1:
            out.append("--\n")
        direct = res.context_kind.get(li, True)
        line = res.lines[li] if li < len(res.lines) else ""
        text = apply_width(line, opt)
        spans = res.line_matches.get(li, []) if direct else []
        text = highlight_line(text, spans, opt)
        col = first_col_for_line(res, li) if direct else None
        out.append(prefix_for_line(res.path, li + 1, col, not direct, opt, include_filename, include_numbers, res.is_stream) + text + "\n")
        prev_li = li
    return "".join(out)


def format_vimgrep(res: FileResult, opt: Options) -> str:
    out: List[str] = []
    if res.is_binary:
        if res.has_match:
            out.append(f"Binary file {res.path} matches.\n")
        return "".join(out)
    if opt.invert:
        for li in res.selected_lines:
            line = res.lines[li]
            out.append(f"{res.path}:{li+1}:1:{line}\n")
        return "".join(out)
    for li, col, _mtext in res.only_matches:
        # For multiline matches ag reports the ending line/column oddly; approximate with start.
        line = res.lines[li] if li < len(res.lines) else ""
        out.append(f"{res.path}:{li+1}:{col}:{line}\n")
    return "".join(out)


def format_ackmate(res: FileResult, opt: Options, include_header: bool) -> str:
    out: List[str] = []
    if include_header:
        out.append(f":{res.path}\n")
    if res.is_binary:
        return "".join(out)
    # One line per matched line, 0-based columns and lengths for all matches on that line.
    for li in sorted(res.line_matches.keys()):
        spans = res.line_matches[li]
        if not spans:
            continue
        specs = ",".join(f"{s} {e-s}" for s, e in spans)
        out.append(f"{li+1};{specs}:{res.lines[li]}\n")
    return "".join(out)


def print_filename_record(path: str, opt: Options):
    end = "\0" if opt.null else "\n"
    sys.stdout.write(path + end)


def print_count_record(res: FileResult, opt: Options, single_file_mode: bool):
    if opt.filename and not single_file_mode and not res.is_stream:
        sys.stdout.write(f"{res.path}:{res.match_count}\n")
    else:
        sys.stdout.write(f"{res.match_count}\n")


def stat_path_error(path: str, opt: Options):
    if opt.silent:
        return
    sys.stderr.write(f"ERR: Error stat()ing: {path}\n")
    sys.stderr.write(f"ERR: Error opening directory {path}: No such file or directory\n")


def open_dir_error(path: str, err: OSError, opt: Options):
    if opt.silent:
        return
    sys.stderr.write(f"ERR: Error opening directory {path}: {err.strerror}\n")


def walk_directory(root_arg: str, opt: Options, global_rules: List[IgnoreRule]) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[str, str, str]], bool]:
    """Return (abs_path, display_path, raw_path) for candidate files, plus whether any errors occurred."""
    files: List[Tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    had_error = False
    root_arg_norm = root_arg.rstrip("/") if root_arg not in ("/", "./") else root_arg
    if root_arg_norm == "":
        root_arg_norm = root_arg
    root_abs = os.path.abspath(root_arg_norm)
    root_raw = root_arg_norm if root_arg_norm != "" else "."
    root_display = strip_display(root_raw.rstrip("/"))
    if root_display == "./": root_display = "."

    # Stat with following symlinks for explicit roots.
    try:
        st = os.stat(root_arg_norm)
    except OSError:
        stat_path_error(root_arg_norm, opt)
        return files, True
    if stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode) or stat.S_ISLNK(os.lstat(root_arg_norm).st_mode):
        # Explicit files are searched regardless of hidden/ignore/type (type filter and G still apply below).
        raw = root_raw
        disp = strip_display(root_raw)
        files.append((root_abs, disp, raw))
        return files, False
    if not stat.S_ISDIR(st.st_mode):
        return files, False

    disable_ign = should_disable_ignores(opt)

    def load_local_rules(dir_abs: str) -> List[IgnoreRule]:
        if disable_ign:
            return []
        rules: List[IgnoreRule] = []
        rules.extend(load_ignore_file(os.path.join(dir_abs, ".ignore"), dir_abs))
        if not opt.skip_vcs_ignores:
            rules.extend(load_ignore_file(os.path.join(dir_abs, ".gitignore"), dir_abs))
            rules.extend(load_ignore_file(os.path.join(dir_abs, ".hgignore"), dir_abs))
            rules.extend(load_ignore_file(os.path.join(dir_abs, ".git", "info", "exclude"), dir_abs))
        return rules

    def rec(dir_abs: str, rel: str, depth_left: int, inherited: List[IgnoreRule], is_root: bool):
        nonlocal had_error
        rules = inherited + load_local_rules(dir_abs)
        try:
            entries = list(os.scandir(dir_abs))
        except OSError as e:
            open_dir_error(join_display(root_display, rel) if rel else root_arg_norm, e, opt)
            had_error = True
            return
        dirs = []
        regulars = []
        for ent in entries:
            name = ent.name
            child_rel = f"{rel}/{name}" if rel else name
            raw = join_raw(root_raw, child_rel)
            disp = join_display(root_display, child_rel)
            abs_p = ent.path
            # Hidden children are skipped unless enabled; explicit root itself was already accepted.
            if not (opt.hidden or opt.unrestricted) and is_hidden_name(name):
                continue
            try:
                is_dir = ent.is_dir(follow_symlinks=opt.follow)
                is_file = ent.is_file(follow_symlinks=opt.follow)
                is_link = ent.is_symlink()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if is_link and not opt.follow:
                continue
            if is_ignored(global_rules + rules, os.path.abspath(abs_p), raw, name, is_dir):
                continue
            if is_dir:
                if not opt.norecurse and (depth_left != 0):
                    next_depth = depth_left - 1 if depth_left > 0 else depth_left
                    dirs.append((abs_p, child_rel, next_depth, rules))
            elif is_file:
                regulars.append((os.path.abspath(abs_p), disp, raw))
        # ag's single-worker order is directory subtrees first, then files in directory order.
        for d_abs, d_rel, d_depth, d_rules in dirs:
            rec(d_abs, d_rel, d_depth, d_rules, False)
        for item in regulars:
            files.append(item)
    rec(root_abs, "", opt.depth, [], True)
    return files, had_error


def stdin_is_search_stream() -> bool:
    try:
        st = os.fstat(0)
    except OSError:
        return False
    if os.isatty(0):
        return False
    mode = st.st_mode
    return stat.S_ISFIFO(mode) or stat.S_ISREG(mode)


def collect_files(paths: List[str], opt: Options, global_rules: List[IgnoreRule]) -> Tuple[List[Tuple[str, str, str]], bool]:
    files: List[Tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    had_error = False
    for p in paths:
        fs, err = walk_directory(p, opt, global_rules)
        files.extend(fs)
        had_error = had_error or err
    return files, had_error


def should_scan_file(abs_path: str, display: str, raw: str, opt: Options, file_re: Optional[re.Pattern]) -> bool:
    if file_re is not None:
        # Ag applies this to the raw path used internally (often with leading ./ for . roots).
        if not file_re.search(raw):
            return False
    if not file_type_matches(display, opt):
        return False
    return True


def run_filename_search(opt: Options, paths: List[str]) -> int:
    assert opt.file_name_pattern is not None
    try:
        file_re = re.compile(opt.file_name_pattern, effective_flags(opt.file_name_pattern, opt))
    except re.error as e:
        sys.stderr.write(regex_error_message(e, opt.file_name_pattern))
        return 2
    global_rules = build_global_ignores(opt)
    files, had_error = collect_files(paths, opt, global_rules)
    matched = False
    for abs_p, disp, raw in files:
        if opt.type_filters and not file_type_matches(disp, opt):
            continue
        if file_re.search(raw):
            print_filename_record(disp, opt)
            matched = True
    return 0 if matched else 1


def debug_prelude(pattern: str, opt: Options):
    if not opt.debug:
        return
    home = os.environ.get("HOME", "")
    if home:
        sys.stdout.write(f"DEBUG: Found user's home dir: {home}\n")
    sys.stdout.write(f"DEBUG: Query is {pattern}\n")
    sys.stdout.write("DEBUG: PCRE Version: 8.39 2016-06-14\n")


def run_search(opt: Options, pattern: str, paths: List[str]) -> int:
    if pattern == "" and not opt.files_with_matches:
        if not opt.silent:
            sys.stderr.write("ERR: Error: No query. What do you want to search for?\n")
        return 1
    regex_pat = prepare_pattern(pattern, opt)
    try:
        regex = re.compile(regex_pat, effective_flags(pattern, opt))
    except re.error as e:
        sys.stderr.write(regex_error_message(e, regex_pat if not opt.literal else pattern))
        return 2
    file_re = None
    if opt.file_search_regex is not None:
        try:
            file_re = re.compile(opt.file_search_regex, effective_flags(opt.file_search_regex, opt))
        except re.error as e:
            sys.stderr.write(regex_error_message(e, opt.file_search_regex))
            return 2

    debug_prelude(pattern, opt)
    start = time.time()
    global_rules = build_global_ignores(opt)
    use_stdin = False
    if not paths:
        if stdin_is_search_stream():
            use_stdin = True
        else:
            paths = ["."]
    single_file_mode = False
    results: List[FileResult] = []
    had_error = False

    if use_stdin:
        data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
        res = analyze_text(data, "", "", regex, opt, is_stream=True, binary=False)
        results.append(res)
        single_file_mode = True
    else:
        files, had_error = collect_files(paths, opt, global_rules)
        # single file mode if exactly one command-line path and it stats as a regular/symlinked file
        if len(paths) == 1:
            try:
                st = os.stat(paths[0].rstrip("/") if paths[0] not in ("/", "./") else paths[0])
                if stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
                    single_file_mode = True
            except OSError:
                pass
        for abs_p, disp, raw in files:
            if not should_scan_file(abs_p, disp, raw, opt, file_re):
                continue
            data = read_file_bytes(abs_p, opt)
            if data is None:
                had_error = True
                continue
            binary = b"\0" in data
            if binary and not opt.search_binary:
                continue
            if binary:
                res = search_binary_file(data, disp, raw, regex, opt)
            else:
                res = analyze_text(data, disp, raw, regex, opt, is_stream=False, binary=False)
            results.append(res)

    # -l with empty query prints all searched files.
    if pattern == "" and opt.files_with_matches:
        any_printed = False
        for res in results:
            if res.searched:
                print_filename_record(res.path, opt)
                any_printed = True
        return 0 if any_printed else 1

    total_matches = sum(r.match_count for r in results if r.searched)
    files_with = sum(1 for r in results if r.searched and r.has_match)
    files_searched = sum(1 for r in results if r.searched)
    bytes_searched = sum(r.bytes_len for r in results if r.searched)

    if opt.files_with_matches:
        matched_any = False
        for res in results:
            if res.searched and res.has_match:
                print_filename_record(res.path, opt)
                matched_any = True
        for res in results:
            if res.too_many and not opt.silent:
                sys.stderr.write(f"ERR: Too many matches in {res.path}. Skipping the rest of this file.\n")
        return 0 if matched_any else 1
    if opt.files_without_matches:
        matched_any = False
        for res in results:
            if res.searched and not res.has_match:
                print_filename_record(res.path, opt)
                matched_any = True
        return 0 if matched_any else 1
    if opt.count:
        any_nonzero = False
        for res in results:
            if res.searched:
                print_count_record(res, opt, single_file_mode)
                if res.match_count:
                    any_nonzero = True
        for res in results:
            if res.too_many and not opt.silent:
                sys.stderr.write(f"ERR: Too many matches in {res.path}. Skipping the rest of this file.\n")
        return 0 if any_nonzero else 1

    heading_mode, break_mode = effective_group(opt)
    if single_file_mode:
        heading_mode = False
    # ackmate/vimgrep/stats-only have their own formatting.
    printed_any = False
    if not opt.stats_only:
        if opt.ackmate:
            multi_header = not single_file_mode and len([r for r in results if r.has_match]) > 1
            first = True
            for res in results:
                if not res.has_match:
                    continue
                if not first and multi_header:
                    sys.stdout.write("\n")
                s = format_ackmate(res, opt, include_header=multi_header)
                sys.stdout.write(s)
                printed_any = printed_any or bool(s)
                first = False
        elif opt.vimgrep:
            for res in results:
                if not res.has_match:
                    continue
                s = format_vimgrep(res, opt)
                sys.stdout.write(s)
                printed_any = printed_any or bool(s)
        else:
            first_file = True
            for res in results:
                if not res.has_match and not (opt.print_all_files and heading_mode):
                    continue
                if heading_mode and opt.filename and not res.is_stream:
                    if not first_file and break_mode:
                        sys.stdout.write("\n")
                    sys.stdout.write(colorize(opt.color_path, res.path, opt) + "\n")
                    s = "" if not res.has_match else format_normal_result(res, opt, single_file_mode, heading_mode=True)
                    sys.stdout.write(s)
                    printed_any = printed_any or res.has_match or opt.print_all_files
                else:
                    if not first_file and break_mode:
                        sys.stdout.write("\n")
                    s = format_normal_result(res, opt, single_file_mode, heading_mode=False)
                    sys.stdout.write(s)
                    printed_any = printed_any or bool(s)
                first_file = False

    for res in results:
        if res.too_many and not opt.silent:
            sys.stderr.write(f"ERR: Too many matches in {res.path}. Skipping the rest of this file.\n")

    if opt.stats or opt.stats_only:
        elapsed = time.time() - start
        sys.stdout.write(f"{total_matches} matches\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"{files_with} files contained matches\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"{files_searched} files searched\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"{bytes_searched} bytes searched\n")
        sys.stdout.write(f"{elapsed:.6f} seconds\n")

    # If there were matches, return success even with path errors. print-all-files also returns success when headings printed.
    if total_matches > 0 or (opt.print_all_files and printed_any):
        return 0
    return 1


def main(argv: List[str]) -> int:
    try:
        opt, pattern, paths, early = parse_args(argv)
    except AgError as e:
        return print_usage_error(e)
    if early is not None:
        return early
    if opt.file_name_pattern is not None:
        return run_filename_search(opt, paths)
    if pattern is None:
        sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
        return 1
    return run_search(opt, pattern, paths)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
    except BrokenPipeError:
        try:
            sys.stdout.close()
        except Exception:
            pass
        sys.exit(1)
